title: India Face New Zealand In Auckland ODI Opener With Morning Rain Forecast
excerpt: The series opens Wednesday, November 4 at Eden Park, with forecasts pointing to morning showers clearing before the 2:00 p.m. local start and no major interruption expected.
body:
• The first ODI is on Wednesday, November 4, 2026 at Eden Park, Auckland, starting at 2:00 p.m. local time (7:30 a.m. IST, toss 7:00 a.m. IST) — 6:00 p.m. Pacific on Tuesday in the United States.
  • Forecasts differ in detail but agree rain is unlikely to cause a major interruption: one AccuWeather-based forecast puts morning rain probability at 56%, with afternoon and evening expected to remain largely clear.
  • New Zealand will be without Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman for the series, according to CricketAddictor, while India are without Jasprit Bumrah, who has been rested, and Prasidh Krishna.
  • In India, the match is on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV, according to both previews.

India and New Zealand open their five-match one-day international series at Eden Park in Auckland on Wednesday, November 4, with forecasts suggesting morning showers should clear before play begins.

The match is scheduled to start at 2:00 p.m. local time, or 7:30 a.m. IST, with the toss at 7:00 a.m. IST, according to the Times of India weather report reproduced by Jammu News Portal. Shubman Gill will captain India and Mitchell Santner will lead New Zealand, the report said.

What the weather forecast actually says

This is a forecast, not a result. According to the AccuWeather forecast details cited in that report, Auckland has a 56% probability of rain during the morning. Conditions are then expected to improve, with the afternoon and evening forecast to remain largely clear, temperatures around 19 degrees Celsius at the start of play and falling to approximately 17 degrees Celsius in the evening.

A separate preview by CricketAddictor gave a more settled outlook for match hours, forecasting sunny weather, temperatures between 17 and 21 degrees Celsius, southeast winds of 6-10 km/h and no significant rain threat. Both accounts point in the same direction for readers planning to watch: a wet morning in Auckland does not, on current forecasts, mean a washed-out match.

Team news for the opener

CricketAddictor reported that New Zealand will be without Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman, who have been ruled out of the entire series due to injuries, with Henry Nicholls and Tim Seifert joining the squad as replacements. It also reported that Devon Conway is unavailable for the opening ODI after suffering a concussion in a training-session collision, and that Matt Henry's availability would depend on a fitness assessment.

For India, the same preview said Jasprit Bumrah has been rested for the series and Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out after failing to secure fitness clearance following a hamstring injury, with Auqib Nabi joining the squad for the first three ODIs as his replacement. Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return to the 50-over setup, it said.

Gill will captain India in the first three matches, according to the reports, with the series then continuing in Wellington on November 7, Hamilton on November 10 and Mount Maunganui on November 13 and November 15, according to the schedule in the weather report.

What Eden Park could produce

Eden Park has traditionally offered a surface that encourages batting, with a relatively flat pitch and shorter boundaries, according to the weather report, although fast bowlers can find opportunities with the new ball. CricketAddictor made a similar assessment, noting short straight boundaries and some swing and extra bounce early before batters can take control once settled.

The venue staged a high-scoring fourth T20I, when New Zealand scored 259 for 7 and beat India by 87 runs, the weather report said. CricketAddictor noted India won that T20I series 3-2 overall.

How to watch

Indian viewers can watch the first ODI live on Sony Sports Network television channels, with online streaming on the Sony LIV app and website, according to both previews. For U.S. readers, that is Tuesday evening — 6:00 p.m. Pacific and 9:00 p.m. Eastern — but the sources listed only India broadcast details and did not confirm a U.S. broadcaster.

On Tuesday's forecasts, fans should expect play, keeping the morning-rain caveat in mind.
